# Review finding: client enforces unreleased protocol field against released provider (P0, python, enhanced-settings task 1)

Pattern: A client increment in an independently-releasable client/provider pair made a new response field mandatory (`response.get("applied") is not True` → raise) before the provider that emits it was released. The supported provider (`eval-release`) writes the settings and returns only `{"ok": True}`, so every ordinary save raises after the values have already been persisted. That is a false failure and breaks backward compatibility.

Compounding pattern: the only unit test's stub was updated to the new provider's response shape. The legacy shape was no longer tested, so the suite passed while the compatibility contract was broken.

Guidance: When adding protocol fields in staged client/provider increments, treat the missing field as legacy-compatible (or gate strictness on provider-advertised capability). Keep a test with the released provider's exact response shape.
